observations: Photo 0 shows a Nikon-branded DSLR body (Nikon logo on top/front).
Photo 0 lens mount area is visible; no lens is clearly shown attached.
Photo 0 has a visible model marking that appears to read D7000 on the right side of the body.
Photo 1 also shows a Nikon-branded DSLR body with the same D7000 marking appearance.
Photo 1 shows the camera being held; a lens cap is visible in the foreground, but no lens is clearly attached.
Both photos show the camera in front of damaged cardboard packaging with Nikon text; no accessories (batteries/case) are clearly shown.

claims.claim: The camera is working perfectly fine.
claims.evidence: No photo shows the camera powered on, recording, or displaying any live screen/menu.

claims.claim: I am selling with 2 batteries and a silicone case.
claims.evidence: Photos show the camera body and packaging, but no batteries or silicone case are visible.
Photos show Nikon branding on the camera body (photo 0 and photo 1), not Canon.

risks.risk: Brand/model mismatch: seller says Canon, but photos show Nikon D7000. This can mean wrong item or bait-and-switch.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of the exact camera’s front/back with the LCD/menu powered on and the model name visible, plus a close-up of the brand/logo.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a Nikon D7000 body with unknown condition (worst case: not confirmed working).

risks.risk: Functionality not proven (shutter, autofocus, buttons, ports, sensor, and LCD).
risks.proof: Video clip: power on + menu navigation + take a short video/photo and show the resulting image on the LCD.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not working/untested until proven.

risks.risk: Missing lens or accessories: photos do not clearly show a lens attached; batteries/case not shown.
risks.proof: Photo checklist: show all included items laid out (2 batteries, charger if any, silicone case, lens if included) with close-ups of labels/contacts.
risks.if_unproven: Price as camera body only, with batteries/case not included.

risks.risk: Physical condition: packaging is damaged; camera may have hidden dents/scratches or wear not visible in these angles.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of: lens mount contacts, sensor area (if accessible), all sides/corners, and LCD screen for cracks.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used with possible cosmetic wear.

proof_requests: Power-on video showing the LCD/menu and a captured photo/video playback (to confirm working).
Close-up photo of the model/serial area and brand/logo (to confirm Nikon D7000 is the exact item).
Photos of the included items laid out: 2 batteries (with labels), silicone case, and charger (if any).
Photos of lens mount and all ports/buttons, plus LCD close-up for cracks/scratches.
response.reason: The photos clearly show a Nikon D7000 body, contradicting the seller’s Canon claim, and the key claims (working perfectly fine; includes 2 batteries and a silicone case) are not verifiable from the images. Proof is needed before pricing confidently.
